title: Garufile
description: One Garu agent: what it does, when it runs, which tools it gets and what it may do with them. https://garuagents.com

name.description: The agent's name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is what you call it, and its folder under agents/.

description.description: What it does, in one line; shown under its name.

language.description: What it writes to you in, as a code (es, pt-BR); it gets the date in that language too. Unset: English.

memory.description: A small notebook it keeps between runs (garu.remember and garu.forget, policed like any tool; you read and edit it on its page).

paused.description: Kept on the schedule but skipped, until you resume it.

persona.description: Its face and one line of character; what it may do is the policy.

kind.description: Its face in the control room: owl (watcher), fox (messenger), turtle (keeper), bee (worker), cat (reader), octopus (planner), rabbit (runner), bear (guardian), frog (connector), penguin (organizer), raccoon (tinkerer), whale (deep reader).

tagline.description: One line of character, shown under its name.

model.description: provider/model, like gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite, anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5, openai/gpt-5-mini or ollama/qwen3:8b.

prompt.description: The job, as the model reads it. Garu adds the date, your name and the tools on its own.

tools.description: The MCP tool servers it may use: a command Garu runs, or a URL it connects to. Empty: it can only think and reply.

name.description: The server's name in rules and in the log: lowercase, digits, - or _. Tools are "<name>.<tool>".

command.description: The program that runs the MCP server (node, npx, python…).

args.description: Its arguments; ${VAR} reads a value from .env.

env.description: Environment variables for the server; ${VAR} reads a value from .env, so secrets never sit here.

auth.description: oauth: Garu signs in for it once (garu auth, or the agent's page) and hands it a short-lived access token at the start of each run.

oauth.description: Your own OAuth client, for a server that does not hand one out.

clientId.description: Your OAuth client id; ${VAR} reads it from .env.

clientSecret.description: Your OAuth client secret, as ${VAR} from .env; never written here.

scopes.description: The permissions the sign-in asks for (the scope).

authorizationParams.description: Extra sign-in parameters, like Google's access_type: offline so runs can refresh the token without you.

issuer.description: Who you sign in with, like https://accounts.google.com. A local server needs it; a remote one finds it on its own.

headers.description: Static headers, like an API key as ${VAR} from .env.

auth.description: oauth: Garu signs in to it once (garu auth) and keeps the tokens.

oauth.description: Your own OAuth client, when the server needs one.

clientId.description: Your OAuth client id; ${VAR} reads it from .env.

clientSecret.description: Your OAuth client secret, as ${VAR} from .env; never written here.

scopes.description: The permissions the sign-in asks for (the scope).

authorizationParams.description: Extra sign-in parameters, like Google's access_type: offline so runs can refresh the token without you.

issuer.description: Who you sign in with, like https://accounts.google.com. A local server needs it; a remote one finds it on its own.

triggers.description: When it runs: a cron schedule, a webhook door, or only when told.

cron.description: A schedule (minute hour day month weekday), in this computer's time zone; runs while the control room is up with --up or as the login service.

webhook.description: A door: POST /api/agents/<agent>/hooks/<name> on the control room starts a run, with the body's message as its input.

manual.description: Runs when told: Run now, a message, garu run.

policy.description: The rules in front of every tool call, read top to bottom; the first match wins, and a call no rule matches asks you.

tool.description: A glob over "<server>.<tool>": "gmail.send", "fs.*", "*". The first rule whose glob and conditions match a call decides it.

action.description: allow: the call goes through on its own. ask: it waits for your approval in the inbox. block: it is refused, and a tool no rule can ever allow is not shown to the model.

when.description: Conditions on the call's arguments, by dotted path ("to", "recipients.length"); every one must hold for the rule to match.

eq.description: The argument equals this value (deep equality for lists and objects).

neq.description: The argument differs from this value.

gt.description: The argument is a number greater than this.

gte.description: The argument is a number greater than or equal to this.

lt.description: The argument is a number less than this.

lte.description: The argument is a number less than or equal to this.

matches.description: The argument, as text, matches this regular expression (JavaScript syntax; no inline modifiers).

ignoreCase.description: For matches: upper and lower case count the same.

in.description: The argument is one of these values.

exists.description: true: the argument is present; false: it is absent.

reason.description: Why, in your words: shown on the review card, in the log and in the push.

maxTurns.description: At most this many model turns in a run, so it can never loop forever.

budget.description: The money guard: a cap per run, a cap on runs a day, your own prices.

maxCostUsd.description: A run stops before its estimated cost crosses this many dollars.

maxRunsPerDay.description: At most this many runs a day, whatever starts them; a run the network cut off does not count.

pricing.description: Your own price for this model, in dollars per million tokens (both 0 on a free tier); otherwise Garu's table.

modelOptions.description: Knobs for the model: temperature, maxOutputTokens, thinkingBudget, and Ollama's own options as they are. A key a provider has no place for is left out.

sandbox.description: Run every tool server inside its own Docker container. Omit to run them on this computer; set (even {}) to contain them.

image.description: The Docker image with the tool servers in it; garu sandbox build makes the default one.

network.description: none: no network at all. bridge: normal outbound internet.

workspace.description: A folder on this computer mounted read-write at /workspace inside the container.

container.description: Where it appears inside the container (an absolute path).

memory.description: Memory for the container, like 512m or 2g.
